paper: Pascoe B, Schiaffino F, Murray S, et al. (2020) Genomic epidemiology of Campylobacter jejuni associated with asymptomatic pediatric infection in the Peruvian Amazon. PLoS Negl Trop Dis 14(8):e0008533.

open_questions.q: Are Peru-dominant clonal complexes CC353, CC362, and CC354 genuinely endemic to Peru / the Amazon basin, or does their apparent 'local restriction' reflect chronic under-sampling of South American, sub-Saharan African, and South-East Asian C. jejuni in pubMLST relative to Northern-Hemisphere clinical surveillance?
open_questions.basis: This rerun confirmed the paper's finding that CC353 (15/62), CC362 (11/62), and CC354 (8/62) dominate the Iquitos pediatric cohort while globally-dominant CC21 (3/62) and CC45 (4/62) are minority contributors. But the contrast is defined against pubMLST's opportunistic global reference set, which is heavily biased toward Europe/North America clinical surveillance and where 15/62 of our own isolates already re-typed under DB drift (8 untyped, 4 novel STs).
open_questions.next_steps: Query pubMLST for the geographic distribution of every isolate ever assigned to CC353/CC362/CC354; stratify by continent and collection year; test whether CC353/CC362/CC354 are truly geographically restricted or merely under-reported outside South America. Cross-check against Enterobase Campylobacter and any published Brazilian/Bolivian/Ecuadorian genomic surveillance data. A CC being rare in pubMLST is not the same as a CC being rare on Earth.

open_questions.q: How well does pubMLST-based host-source attribution (poultry vs livestock vs human) actually classify Peruvian Amazon C. jejuni isolates, given that the source-attribution training data is dominated by UK/US poultry-farm and clinical isolates and has minimal Amazon-basin farm-side or environmental representation?
open_questions.basis: The paper attributes source using pubMLST ecology annotations; this rerun substituted ST-diversity + Mash-distance summaries per aetiology group and reproduced the aetiology split (31 sympt / 28 asympt / 3 unknown) but did not independently validate the source-attribution accuracy. In the Iquitos setting, backyard-chicken, guinea-pig, and river-water exposures are common but have no matched genomic reference panel.
open_questions.next_steps: Collect matched farm-side chicken, guinea-pig, and household-environment C. jejuni isolates from the same Iquitos catchment; re-run source attribution with a locally-augmented reference panel; measure how classification confidence and category assignments change vs the pubMLST-only baseline. Report per-source recall and confusion; publish the augmented reference set.

open_questions.q: In a resource-limited-setting cohort like Iquitos, what is the true C. jejuni carriage prevalence and CC composition once sampling bias, culture-based recovery bias (fastidious growth), and pediatric-only enrolment are corrected for --- and does the 31 symptomatic / 28 asymptomatic / 3 unknown split hold at the community level?
open_questions.basis: This rerun reproduced the 31/28/3 split from the paper's S6, and confirmed asymptomatic polyphyly (17 STs across 28 asymptomatic isolates; within-group Mash distance 0.0180 vs symptomatic 0.0164). But the enrolment window, age band, and culture-based recovery pipeline all shape which isolates are captured; the paper does not (and this rerun could not) estimate the fraction of true community C. jejuni carriage missed at the culture step.
open_questions.next_steps: Complement culture with metagenomic or qPCR-based C. jejuni detection on a matched stool sub-set to estimate culture-recovery sensitivity; extend sampling to household adult contacts to test whether asymptomatic polyphyly is a pediatric-specific phenomenon or a population-level baseline; report CC composition stratified by age band and by culture-positive vs metagenomics-positive.

open_questions.q: Are fluoroquinolone (gyrA T86I) and tetracycline (tetO) resistance-marker prevalences in South American pediatric C. jejuni systematically different from Northern-Hemisphere surveillance isolates, and does the observed low tetracycline prevalence in the Iquitos cohort (10-11/62, ~16-18%) reflect a genuine regional signal or ABRicate cutoff sensitivity?
open_questions.basis: This rerun found tetracycline 10/62 (paper: 11/62; agreement within +/-1), aminoglycoside 0/62 (exact), but beta-lactam 26 vs 32 --- a 6-isolate gap traced to ABRicate's default 80/80 identity/coverage cutoff clipping borderline blaOXA-61 hits. Fluoroquinolone gyrA T86I was not separately tabulated in the S5 summary re-used here as ground truth. Regional AMR comparability is therefore only partially established.
open_questions.next_steps: Re-run ABRicate at multiple identity/coverage cutoffs (80/80, 90/90, 95/60) and separately genotype gyrA T86I directly from the assemblies; compare Peru marker prevalence against published pediatric C. jejuni AMR profiles from Bangladesh, Kenya, and Peruvian Lima cohorts; where possible cross-check against phenotypic disk-diffusion or MIC data from the same isolates to separate genotype-only signal from actionable phenotype.

open_questions.q: Do virulence-gene profiles (CDT operon cdtA/B/C, cadF, ciaB, wlaN, cst-II, LOS locus class) segregate cleanly by symptomatic vs asymptomatic carriage in the Iquitos cohort, and if not, what alternative mechanism (host factors, co-infection, exposure dose, prior sensitisation) accounts for the paper's central finding that asymptomatic and symptomatic isolates are phylogenetically indistinguishable?
open_questions.basis: This rerun reproduced the paper's polyphyly finding (17 STs across 28 asymptomatic isolates; within-group Mash 0.0180 >= symptomatic 0.0164) and used ABRicate against VFDB but did not publish a per-gene symptomatic-vs-asymptomatic virulence-profile comparison. The paper reports the strains are 'not a single lineage' but does not fully close the loop on why genetically-similar strains cause disease in one host and not another.
open_questions.next_steps: Extract per-isolate VFDB gene-presence matrix from the deposited abricate/vfdb.tsv; run Fisher/GWAS-style association of each virulence gene against symptomatic/asymptomatic status; separately test LOS class (A vs B vs C) and cst-II sialylation status; where signals appear, cross-reference with cohort metadata (age, breastfeeding status, prior C. jejuni exposure, co-infection) to distinguish pathogen-side from host-side drivers of the polyphyly finding.
